caveats: a name shown here comes from another program that declared the same discriminator, not from this one — treat it as a strong hint, not a fact. `ix_<hex>` means no published IDL anywhere declares it.
an account marked `constant` was the same address in every sample, which usually means a fixed global — but a program used by only one caller will look that way too.

argument layout is NOT decoded. `argsHex` below is the observed bytes after the discriminator — pass them back verbatim as `argsHex` on the instruction spec. Without that the transaction carries the right accounts and an EMPTY payload, which the program will reject.
body.howToUse: pass this whole object as `idl` to /tx/build or /tx/batch. Account names are positional (`account_0`...) because transactions do not carry names; anything with a `pda` block is derived for you, the rest you supply.
